title: Abstract associativity assembly for pairings with a partial tensorator
statement: Let C,D be monoidal categories, S:C to D a functor, and P a predicate closed under tensor product. For each P-object L and arbitrary M let mu(L,M):S(L) tensor S(M) to S(L tensor M) be natural in arrows between P-objects on the left and arbitrary arrows on the right. Suppose these comparisons satisfy the canonical associator square with specified arrows A(L,M,N). For arbitrary ordinary pairings f,g,h,k,a with P(L),P(M),P(K) and f tensor 1;g;a = associator;1 tensor h;k, the pairings mu;S(f), etc. satisfy the corresponding equation with A. No invertibility or exactness is assumed.

source.place: Tag 06YU, functorial coherence of tensor pairings; elementary categorical assembly of the canonical comparison squares.

proof.text: Use tensorator naturality on f tensor identity and identity tensor h. Replace the canonical initial composite by the assumed associator square. The remaining tails are S of the given ordinary associativity equation, so functoriality and that equation finish the proof.

theorem flatPairing_associativity_assembly
    {C : Type uC} {D : Type uD} [Category.{vC} C] [Category.{vD} D]
    [MonoidalCategory C] [MonoidalCategory D]
    (S : C ⥤ D) (P : C → Prop)
    (μ : ∀ L M : C, P L → (S.obj L ⊗ S.obj M ⟶ S.obj (L ⊗ M)))
    (A : ∀ L M N : C,
      (S.obj L ⊗ S.obj M) ⊗ S.obj N ⟶ S.obj L ⊗ (S.obj M ⊗ S.obj N))
    (h_tensor : ∀ {L M : C}, P L → P M → P (L ⊗ M))
    (h_natural : ∀ {L L' M M' : C} (f : L ⟶ L') (g : M ⟶ M')
      (hL : P L) (hL' : P L'),
      (S.map f ⊗ₘ S.map g) ≫ μ L' M' hL' = μ L M hL ≫ S.map (f ⊗ₘ g))
    (h_assoc : ∀ (L M N : C) (hL : P L) (hM : P M),
      μ L M hL ▷ S.obj N ≫ μ (L ⊗ M) N (h_tensor hL hM) ≫
          S.map (α_ L M N).hom =
        A L M N ≫ S.obj L ◁ μ M N hM ≫ μ L (M ⊗ N) hL)
    {L M N K Q R T : C} (hL : P L) (hM : P M) (hK : P K)
    (f : L ⊗ M ⟶ K) (g : K ⊗ N ⟶ R) (h : M ⊗ N ⟶ Q)
    (k : L ⊗ Q ⟶ T) (a : R ⟶ T)
    (w : f ▷ N ≫ g ≫ a = (α_ L M N).hom ≫ L ◁ h ≫ k) :
    (μ L M hL ≫ S.map f) ▷ S.obj N ≫
        (μ K N hK ≫ S.map g) ≫ S.map a =
      A L M N ≫ S.obj L ◁ (μ M N hM ≫ S.map h) ≫ (μ L Q hL ≫ S.map k)
